analysis: What changed vs the 7:00 AM brief: the morning's fade turned into a full reversal. The S&P 500 opened +0.29% on the cooler PPI print, then slid all session — by ~10:45 AM ET it was down 0.9% with the Nasdaq 100 down 2% and SPY at $750.43 (-0.88%), near its $747.88 low. Nvidia broke below $160 (-3.86% at $159.77) after the premarket bounce failed twice, and AMD fell 7.2% after a five-session rise, so the chip complex is dragging the tape, not just NVDA. The VIX jumped above 20 (+2.26 vs the 7 AM reading) while the 10-year held ~5.13% — the selloff is equity-led, not a fresh rate spike. Fed's Collins spoke at 9:10 AM ET and declined to comment on the policy outlook, so the three-hike repricing (BofA Dec/Jan/Mar, Goldman Dec plus March) still stands unchallenged until Bowman (10:50 AM ET), Daly (noon) and Jefferson (7 PM) speak. Microsoft is the counterpoint: Teams is restored and the stock is +0.42% even with the outage unresolved and an email backlog still clearing. Apple (+1.13%, new 52-week high $360.83) and Meta (+0.96%) are still holding the tape's green pockets, while GOOGL (-1.33%) and TSLA (-1.98%) joined the fade. Signal vs noise: the PPI relief fading within an hour and the VIX breaking 20 are real — the market is pricing the hiking path over the inflation data. Cerebras +18% and the xAI layoff report are side stories; the IEA surplus call and the outage remain the background context.

headlines.headline: The green open fully reversed by late morning: S&P 500 -0.9%, Nasdaq 100 -2%, Russell 2000 -0.88% as of ~10:43 AM ET. SPY is $750.43 (-0.88% vs Thursday's $757.12 close) after opening at $760.07 and touching a $747.88 low; the Dow is the relative holdout at -0.33%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second leg down after the opening fade means the PPI relief is fully spent — the tape is now trading the Fed hiking path, not the inflation print.

headlines.headline: Nvidia broke below $160, now $159.77 (-3.86%) after opening at $169.91 and touching a $170.00 high; the stock is down ~12% this week and -27.8% over the past month. Earnings are Tue Nov 17 (Kress's first call as interim CEO); consensus expects ~$109.09B revenue (+91% YoY) and ~74% gross margin vs 75% last quarter.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two failed bounces in one session and a break of $160 show sellers are in control into earnings — the governance overhang is now compounding with margin and AI-spending doubts.

headlines.headline: AMD fell 7.2% after a five-session rise, and Cisco fell 2% after lower Q1 gross margins; the renewed chip slide weighed on the Nasdaq. Cerebras is the offset, +18% after lifting its FY26 revenue forecast.
headlines.why_it_matters: The weakness is spreading beyond NVDA into the broader chip complex — a sector-wide AI-valuation reset, not a single-stock story.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's 365 outage is into day two: Microsoft says Teams service health is restored and email delivery is improving, but the incident is not declared resolved and the focus is now clearing the email queue and backlog; no root cause yet and no cyberattack indicated. MSFT is +0.42% at $525.21, recovering from -1.37% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Partial recovery is lifting the stock off its lows, but a second day without a root cause keeps the reliability question open for enterprise customers.

headlines.headline: Fed's Collins spoke at 9:10 AM ET and did not comment on the monetary-policy outlook, saying higher productivity has helped limit some inflation pressures. Bowman speaks at 10:50 AM ET, Daly at noon, Jefferson at 7:00 PM ET. Two-year Treasury yields are headed for their biggest weekly jump in two years.
headlines.why_it_matters: Collins offered no pushback on the three-hike repricing, so the market's next rate signal comes from Bowman's remarks — a hawkish tone would extend the selloff.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split as the tape faded: AAPL hit a new 52-week high of $360.83 and is +1.13% at $358.90; META +0.96% at $629.58 — while GOOGL fell -1.33% to $294.74, TSLA -1.98% to $389.58 after touching $404.40 at the open, and AMZN -0.78% at $265.35.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple and Meta are the only green megacaps left — the rotation that held the tape up at the open is narrowing as the selloff broadens.
